newsitem.title: USA: U.S. firm linked to ValuJet crash leaves Miami.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm linked to ValuJet crash leaves Miami.

text.p: SabreTech Inc, the aircraft maintenance company that handled volatile oxygen canisters suspected of causing the crash of ValuJet Flight 592 near Miami last May, said Thursday it was ending operations in the city.

"We are in the final throes of negotiations for an asset purchase agreement for the Miami facility," said SabreTech attorney Kenneth Quinn, adding the company might announce a sale agreement as soon as Friday.

"It's another sad and tragic chapter in the ValuJet saga, but we are doing everything we can to preserve jobs," Quinn said. SabreTech, one of the nation's largest aircraft maintenance contractors, is a Phoenix, Arizona-based division of Saberliner Corp of St. Louis.

ValuJet Flight 592 plunged into Florida's Everglades near Miami on May 11, killing all 110 passengers and crew. Inspectors believe oxygen canisters improperly packed by SabreTech and loaded aboard the aircraft may have started or fueled a fire in the doomed DC-9's cargo hold.
At its peak around the time of the crash, SabreTech had some 650 employees and contract employees in Miami. That fell to 135 in the wake of the disaster, Quinn said.

"This is the direct result of the continuing adverse publicity and unprecedented investigation following the ValuJet crash," Quinn said. "It has led to a precipitous decline in our customer base in the Miami facility that prevents us from maintaining a viable presence here.
He said the company had no plans to close its facility in Orlando, Florida and noted its large operation in Phoenix was performing well.
